payload.reason: The evidence provides specific reasons why beam search is inadequate, including its inefficiency in handling similar hypotheses and its tendency to prune potentially high-quality outputs.

claims.text: Beam search is inadequate because it uses significant computational resources to explore similar hypotheses, leading to wasted efforts on paths that are ultimately pruned.
Beam search does not handle very similar hypotheses efficiently, which limits its effectiveness in generating diverse outputs.
Increasing the beam size does not significantly improve diversity and can lead to a decrease in the quality of generated text.
Beam search prunes many paths that could yield high-quality outputs, wasting computational resources on less likely nodes.
